papers.title: Oncogenic transformation proceeds through a transient state of cellular plasticity constrained by lineage-specific barriers
papers.authors: Frangou, C., Safina, A., Commane, M., Jadhav, V., Salameh, A., Buckley, B., Singh, P., Luke, J., Diaz, D., Leonova, K., Wang, J., Gurova, K.
papers.abstract: Normal tissues frequently harbor oncogenic mutations without progressing to cancer, but the cellular basis of this resistance remains poorly defined. We asked whether transformation requires selection of a rare, permissive state within normal-like cell populations. Dermal fibroblasts and mammary epithelial cells responded uniformly to combined HRAS-G12V expression and p53 disruption. Cellular barc
summary_bullets: Normal cells can harbor oncogenic mutations without transforming; transformation requires passing through a rare, transient plastic cell state.
Dermal fibroblasts and mammary epithelial cells respond differently to HRAS-G12V + p53 loss, revealing lineage-specific barriers to transformation.
Cellular barcoding was used to track which subpopulations become permissive to oncogenic transformation.

papers.title: Invasion status stratifies the composition of the human pancreatic cancer perineural niche
papers.authors: Hussain, Z., Yarlagadda, D. V. K., Li, Q., Tezcan, N., Stupakov, P., Sadatrezaei, G., Wong, R. J., Massague, J., Tarcan, Z., Basturk, O., Deborde, S., Leslie, C. S., Sherman, M. H.
papers.abstract: The peripheral nervous system innervates the pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) microenvironment, and perineural invasion (PNI), the invasion of cancer cells in and around nerves, correlates with metastatic burden and poor outcomes. Though PDAC innervation is near universal and the majority of PDAC patients harbor PNI, the cellular and molecular composition of the heterocellular perineural ni
summary_bullets: Perineural invasion (PNI) is common in PDAC and linked to worse outcomes, but its cellular composition was unclear.
The study profiles how invasion status changes the cell types present in the perineural niche.
Findings point to niche-specific targets tied to nerve invasion in pancreatic cancer.

papers.title: A patient-derived xenograft model of FUS::TFCP2 intraosseous rhabdomyosarcoma reveals chemoresistance and differential sensitivity to ALK inhibitors
papers.authors: Chauhan, S., Jones, K., Krajbich, V. A., Smith, B., McCallister, C., Bui, T., Smith, R., Woltjer, R. L., Wangsiricharoen, S., Ramsay, D., Davare, M. A.
papers.abstract: TFCP2-rearranged rhabdomyosarcoma is an exceptionally rare and highly aggressive malignancy driven by TFCP2 gene fusions and associated with a dismal clinical prognosis. Because standardized treatment regimens are lacking, developing representative preclinical models is critical for identifying effective therapies. Here, we present a case of a 29-year-old male with rapidly progressive, metastatic
summary_bullets: Established a patient-derived xenograft model from a rare, aggressive FUS::TFCP2-fusion rhabdomyosarcoma case.
The model reveals resistance to standard chemotherapy.
ALK inhibitors show differential sensitivity, suggesting a targetable vulnerability.

papers.title: SWI/SNF Alterations Define a Chromatin-Dependent Subtype of Urothelial Carcinoma
papers.authors: Feng, B.-J., Fatema, K., Nix, D. A., Atkinson, A., Caparas, C., Stubben, C. J., Lum, D. H., Parnell, T. J., Carroll, C., Grass, G. D., Graham, L., Singer, E. A., Nepple, K. G., Manojlovic, Z., Kauffman, E., King, J. M., Ghodoussipour, S., Hensley, P., Viscuse, P. V., Ayanambakkam, A., Churchman, M. L., Swami, U., Agarwal, N., Cairns, B., Gupta, S.
papers.abstract: Purpose: SWI/SNF (BAF) chromatin remodeling complex alterations are common in urothelial carcinoma, yet no biomarker-directed therapeutic strategies have been established for this population. We investigated whether BAF alterations delineate a biologically distinct, therapeutically actionable urothelial carcinoma subtype. Experimental Design: We performed integrative genomic and transcriptomic ana
summary_bullets: SWI/SNF (BAF) complex alterations define a distinct, chromatin-dependent subtype of urothelial carcinoma.
Integrative genomic and transcriptomic analysis links BAF alterations to a specific tumor biology.
Findings suggest BAF status could guide future biomarker-driven therapy in bladder cancer.

papers.title: Developmental reversion underlies resistance to immune checkpoint blockade in kidney cancer
papers.authors: Yarlagadda, D. V. K., Wang, Z., Jiang, H., Vuong, L., Sanmiguel, A. L., Yang, C.-Y., Kotecha, R. R., Chen, Y.-B., Hakimi, A. A., Leslie, C. S., Massague, J.
papers.abstract: Despite the clinical success of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in the management of advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), many tumors develop acquired resistance, presumed to arise from a refractory subpopulation of persister cancer cells. Previous studies have provided insights into tumor microenvironment-specific drivers of ICI resistance in ccRCC. However, the extent to which c
summary_bullets: Immune checkpoint inhibitor resistance in ccRCC is linked to tumor cells reverting to an earlier developmental state.
Persister cancer cells adopt this reverted state to evade immune attack despite ICI treatment.
Suggests targeting developmental reversion pathways could resensitize tumors to checkpoint blockade.

papers.title: Dynamic prediction of HIV-related incomplete immune reconstitution: A multicenter, large cohort study using advanced joint modeling.
papers.authors: Liu F, Zhang H, Wang X, Huang J, Shi J, Yang Z, Bao J, Zhao H, Pu C, Wang S, Xu A, Wang M, Yan D, Li Y, Sun R, Sheng H, Yu J, Zhang F, Sun L.
papers.abstract: Incomplete immune reconstitution (IIR) is a serious complication affecting 10 to 40% of people living with HIV (PLWH) despite effective antiretroviral therapy, leading to increased morbidity and mortality. Current risk prediction models rely on single-time point measurements and lack dynamic assessment capabilities. We developed a dynamic joint prediction system for IIR risk (DJPSIIR) using Bayesi
summary_bullets: Incomplete immune reconstitution affects 10-40% of people with HIV despite effective antiretroviral therapy.
Built a dynamic joint-modeling system (DJPSIIR) using repeated measurements instead of single time points.
Aims to give clinicians better, continuously updated risk prediction for IIR.

papers.title: Leveraging IGF signaling to improve the spatial organization and regenerative potential of iPSC-derived vascularized liver organoids.
papers.authors: Kim DH, Lee Y, Kim MJ, Lee AC, Kwon S, Kang KS.
papers.abstract: Liver tissue engineering offers a promising alternative for end-stage liver disease, yet the recreation of functional vasculature remains a major bottleneck to clinical translation. Here, we developed vascularized liver organoids by integrating human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived hepatoblasts and endothelial cells into decellularized scaffolds functionalized with an anti-CD31 aptame
summary_bullets: Engineered vascularized liver organoids from iPSC-derived hepatoblasts and endothelial cells on functionalized scaffolds.
IGF signaling improves spatial organization of the vasculature within the organoid.
Enhances regenerative potential, a step toward liver tissue engineering for end-stage liver disease.

papers.title: Assessing pedestrian responses to autonomous and personal mobility robots in crowded public spaces.
papers.authors: Wojcikiewicz D, Billard A, Paez-Granados D.
papers.abstract: Robots increasingly share spaces with people, supporting delivery services and mobility for the aging populations, yet their ability to share space comfortably lacks understanding and benchmarks for designers and policy-makers. We compared human-robot (HRI) and human-human (HHI) interactions across four real-world crowd datasets spanning Europe, North America, and Asia, using a unified pipeline to
summary_bullets: Compared human-robot and human-human interactions across four real-world crowd datasets on three continents.
Used a unified analysis pipeline to benchmark how pedestrians respond to autonomous/personal mobility robots.
Offers empirical benchmarks to guide robot design and public-space policy.

papers.title: BirdCODE: Detecting bird communication at scale
papers.authors: Fine, A., Hoffman, B., Robinson, D., Miron, M., Alizadeh, M., Chemla, E., Cusimano, M., James, L. S., Keen, S., Matthies, E., Narula, G., Nolasco, I., Geist, M.
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based animal sound identification is regularly applied to large audio datasets for ecological monitoring and citizen science, but existing methods lack the fine temporal resolution required to extract insights into animal communication from these same datasets. Here we introduce Bird Communication Detector (BirdCODE), a deep learning model that detects and classifies the vocalization
summary_bullets: Introduces BirdCODE, a deep learning model for fine-grained, high-temporal-resolution detection of bird vocalizations.
Improves on existing tools that lack the temporal resolution needed to study animal communication in detail.
Enables large-scale bioacoustic monitoring and communication research from existing audio datasets.

papers.title: IMAS resolves perturbation-sensitive regulatory architectures from matched tumour multiomics
papers.authors: Deyang, W., Yamashiro, T., Inubushi, T.
papers.abstract: Tumour single-cell datasets contain weak, sparse and context-restricted regulatory signals that are difficult to distinguish from noise using expression measurements alone. Here we present IMAS, an integrative multiomic augmentation system that learns transferable regulatory structure from a pan-cancer foundation of matched single-cell RNA and chromatin-accessibility profiles and adapts it to data
summary_bullets: IMAS is an integrative multiomic model that learns regulatory structure from matched single-cell RNA + chromatin accessibility data.
Trained on a pan-cancer foundation, then adapted to resolve weak, sparse regulatory signals in individual tumors.
Helps distinguish real perturbation-sensitive regulatory signal from noise in sparse tumor single-cell data.

papers.title: Patient-Derived Liver Cancer Organoids Reflect Tumor Biology and Their Growth Phenotype Correlates with Clinical Outcomes
papers.authors: Kim, Y. S., Go, Y.-H., Kim, H. S., Seo, J., Kim, D. O., Hwang, D.-Y., Yang, W., Lim, J. H.
papers.abstract: Liver cancer remains a major global health burden with high mortality and limited treatment response prediction tools. Patient-derived cancer organoids have emerged as promising preclinical models that recapitulate tumor heterogeneity; however, the biological significance of morphological diversity within established organoids remains poorly characterized in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In this
summary_bullets: Patient-derived liver cancer organoids recapitulate tumor heterogeneity and biology.
Organoid growth phenotype (morphological diversity) correlates with clinical outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma.
Positions organoid growth patterns as a potential predictive biomarker.

papers.title: Spatial remodeling of the thymic stroma with age disrupts niches for T cell selection and tolerance
papers.authors: Tarcevski, A., Dhalla, F., Moore, J., Zuklys, S., Kusch, A., Tchernev, L., Grier, J., Maio, S., Khan, A., Barthlott, T., Deadman, M., Handel, A. E., Byrne, H., Hollander, G.
papers.abstract: Age-associated thymic involution is a major driver of immunosenescence, yet the cellular and spatial mechanisms coordinating age-related thymic remodeling remain incompletely understood. Combining single-cell transcriptomics, chromatin accessibility profiling, and spatial transcriptomics, we generated a spatially resolved multi-omic atlas of the aging mouse thymus. We show that thymic aging is not
summary_bullets: Built a spatially resolved multi-omic atlas of the aging mouse thymus (single-cell + chromatin + spatial transcriptomics).
Age-related thymic involution disrupts stromal niches needed for T cell selection and tolerance.
Links spatial stromal remodeling directly to declining T cell education with age.

papers.title: Multi-modal Graph Integration for Biologically Interpretable Domain Identification Using Spatial Transcriptomics
papers.authors: Lee, S., Wang, G., Kang, K., Chen, J., Kang, M.
papers.abstract: Functional domain identification in spatial transciptomics transforms spatial molecular measurements into mechanistic insights into tissue physiology and pathology. However, the inherent noise and sparsity of gene expression data, along with the locality-biased design of conventional graph-based approaches, fundamentally limit the accurate identification of complex tissue domains. In this study, w
summary_bullets: Introduces a multi-modal graph model to identify tissue domains from spatial transcriptomics more accurately.
Addresses noise, sparsity, and locality bias that limit conventional graph-based domain-finding methods.
Aims to make computational domain identification more biologically interpretable.

papers.title: Graph Machine Learning for Physiological Role Prediction in Protein Contact Networks: A Large-Scale Comparative Study on the Human Proteome
papers.authors: Cervellini, M., Martino, A.
papers.abstract: Proteins are fundamental macromolecules involved in virtually all biological processes. Their physiological roles are tightly linked to their three-dimensional structure, which can be naturally abstracted as Protein Contact Networks (PCNs), i.e., graphs where residues are nodes and edges encode spatial proximity. This representation enables the application of graph machine learning to address the
summary_bullets: Large-scale comparative study applying graph machine learning to Protein Contact Networks across the human proteome.
Represents protein 3D structure as residue-contact graphs to predict physiological roles.
Benchmarks which graph ML approaches best capture structure-function relationships proteome-wide.

papers.title: AI-guided discovery of antimicrobial peptides for urinary tract infections leveraging a new catalogue of the human urinary microbiome
papers.authors: Ke, S., Zingl, F. G., Wang, X.-W., Hale, V. L., Weiss, S. T., Waldor, M., Liu, Y.-Y.
papers.abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are common infections that pose a critical burden on healthcare and society. Despite growing recognition that the human urinary tract harbors its own microbiome, its composition, functional potential, and alterations in UTI remain limited. Here, we leveraged the publicly available whole-metagenome shotgun sequencing data from 450 urinary microbiome samples collected
summary_bullets: Built a new catalogue of the human urinary microbiome from ~450 shotgun metagenomic samples.
Used AI to discover candidate antimicrobial peptides targeting urinary tract infection-associated microbes.
Offers a resource and pipeline for future peptide-based UTI therapeutics.

papers.title: Trajectory Uncertainty Framework (TUF): A Modular Framework for Identifying Transitional and Branch-Point Cell States in Single-Cell Trajectory Analysis
papers.authors: Mahdavifar, M., Mohammadifar, Z., Iranpourtari, T.
papers.abstract: Single-cell trajectory inference methods assign pseudotime coordinates but provide limited information on assignment uncertainty, especially at transitional states and branch points. We introduce the Trajectory Uncertainty Framework (TUF), a modular, downstream approach that defines a 2D uncertainty coordinate system for single-cell data. TUF decomposes local uncertainty into the Temporal Entropy
summary_bullets: Introduces TUF, a framework that quantifies uncertainty in single-cell pseudotime trajectory assignments.
Decomposes uncertainty into components (e.g. "Temporal Entropy") to flag transitional/branch-point cells.
Helps researchers avoid over-interpreting noisy trajectory inference at ambiguous cell states.

papers.title: Distinct cellular phenotypes of language and executive decline in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
papers.authors: Petrescu J, Gouveia Roque C, Jackson CA, Daly AC, Butti Z, Kang K, Casel O, Leung M, Reilly L, Eschbach J, Gebremedhin B, McDade K, Gregory JM, Bonneau R, Smith C, Phatnani H.
papers.abstract: Cognitive manifestations, including impairments in language and executive functions, are seen in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We mapped prefrontal cortex regions from ALS patients by integrating spatial and single-nucleus transcriptomics in a cognitively stratified patient cohort. We uncover that cognitive impairment in ALS is associated with d
summary_bullets: Mapped prefrontal cortex regions in ALS patients using combined spatial and single-nucleus transcriptomics.
Cognitive impairment (language/executive decline) in ALS is associated with distinct cellular changes.
Stratified cohort by cognitive status to link specific cell states to specific symptoms.

papers.title: Divergent impacts of explainable AI for dermatological diagnosis on clinicians versus lay people
papers.authors: Xu X', Hu H, Zhang H, Wang WK, Wang R, Soenksen LR, Badri O, Jafry S, Burger E, Nwandu L, Mehta A, Duhaime EP, Qasim A, Lin H, Pereira JK, Hershon J, Mui P, Gru AA, Elhadad N, Mamykina L, Groh M, Tschandl P, Daneshjou R, Ghassemi M.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly permeating healthcare, from serving as a physician assistant to powering consumer applications. The opacity of AI algorithms makes the ability of humans to interact with AI algorithms challenging. To overcome this limitation, explainable AI (XAI) provides insight into AI decision-making, but evidence suggests that XAI can paradoxically induce bias in th
summary_bullets: Explainable AI (XAI) is meant to make AI decisions more transparent in dermatology diagnosis.
XAI has divergent effects: it can help or paradoxically bias interpretation depending on the user.
Clinicians and lay people respond very differently to the same AI explanations.

papers.title: Follicular Lymphoma Transformation is Characterized by Cytokine-associated Remodeling of Stromal and Macrophage Compartments.
papers.authors: Haradhvala NJ, Yiu SPT, Beckmann L, Sadigh S, Leibowitz Z, Landolsi E, Rivero S, Deng SL, Hu S, Zhang M, Filip D, Pospistle A, Yeo YY, Maurer K, Gustafsson J, Stewart K, Shanmugam V, Van Orden M, Lu WS, Li S, Livak KJ, Qiu H, Basak A, Shalek AK, Danysh BP, McDonough M, Gohil SH, Ren Y, Zhou Y, Neuberg DS, Tyekucheva S, Rodig SJ, Jacobsen ED, Mraz M, Murakami MA, Kurt H, Wu CJ, Getz G, Jiang S, Parry EM.
papers.abstract: Across cancer, one of the most frequent examples of histologic transformation is the evolution of follicular lymphoma (FL) to an aggressive large cell lymphoma. Despite recent progress, understanding of the molecular and cellular underpinnings of transformation remains incomplete. Here, we dissect the interplay of tumor and microenvironment cell populations across transformation through a multimod
summary_bullets: Multimodal profiling dissects tumor-microenvironment interplay during transformation of follicular lymphoma to aggressive large-cell lymphoma.
Transformation is characterized by cytokine-driven remodeling of stromal and macrophage compartments.
Identifies microenvironmental changes as active drivers, not just bystanders, of lymphoma transformation.

papers.title: Identification of pre-existing ubiquitous neoantigen-reactive tumor-infiltrating T-cells in a patient with metastatic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor
papers.authors: Tanis, J.-B., McCann, K., Castaneda-Castro, F. E., Thomas, J., Bailey, A., Singh, P., Currall, E., Chudley, L., Simon, H., Nicholas, B., Cave, J., Takhar, A., Burdak-Rothkamm, S., Schoenberger, S. P., Greenbaum, J., Skipp, P., Vijayanand, P., Seumois, G., Savelyeva, N., Ottensmeier, C.
papers.abstract: BackgroundMutation-derived neoantigens, typically identified in primary tumors, are emerging therapeutic targets for personalized cancer vaccines and adoptive T-cell therapies. However, clinical efficacy of neoantigen-directed therapies in patients with metastatic disease remains limited, partly due to inter-site genetic heterogeneity. We investigated whether ubiquitous neoantigens-derived from mu
summary_bullets: Found tumor-infiltrating T cells reactive to "ubiquitous" neoantigens shared across metastatic sites, not just primary tumor.
These pre-existing T cells were present despite limited clinical efficacy of neoantigen-directed therapies to date.
Suggests targeting ubiquitous neoantigens could improve therapy for metastatic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors.

papers.title: Deep-ultraviolet microscopy reveals biomolecular spatiotemporal intracellular dynamics
papers.authors: Gorti, V., Si, M., Taylor, N., Cicerone, M., Robles, F. E.
papers.abstract: Intracellular dynamics span a broad range of time scales and biomolecular processes, offering insights into cell health, functional state, phenotype, and response to external perturbations. Several label-free optical imaging approaches have been used to capture intracellular dynamics but are limited by spatiotemporal resolution and biomolecular specificity required to distinguish unique subcellula
summary_bullets: Developed a label-free deep-ultraviolet microscopy method to track intracellular biomolecular dynamics.
Overcomes spatiotemporal resolution and specificity limits of existing label-free imaging approaches.
Enables direct observation of subcellular processes without fluorescent labeling.

papers.title: Preclinical Characterization of Hippo pathway inhibition: Insights from Pharmacological and Genetic Studies
papers.authors: Paul, S., Lepherd, M., Hagenbeek, T., Kiyota, S. K., Ning, M., Shi, M., Daniel, B., Ybarra, R., Sims, J., Dey, A.
papers.abstract: The Hippo pathway is an evolutionarily conserved regulator of growth, regeneration, and organ homeostasis, and while its dysregulation is well established in cancer, the effects of inhibiting this pathway on normal tissues are less understood. Here we have systematically investigated the impact of Hippo pathway inhibition by comparing pharmacologic perturbation using a covalent small-molecule TEAD
summary_bullets: Systematically compared pharmacological (TEAD inhibitor) vs. genetic Hippo pathway inhibition in normal tissue.
Hippo's role in cancer is established, but effects of inhibiting it in healthy tissue were unclear.
Characterizes on-target normal-tissue effects relevant to Hippo-targeted drug safety.

papers.title: Hematopoietic stem cell conditioned media induces excessive mitochondrial fission via Drp-1 to target colorectal cancer
papers.authors: Mallick, S., Rai, A. B., Narayana, V. K., Keshava Prasad, T. S., Shenoy, S. P., Bose, B., Biswas, S.
papers.abstract: Mitochondria, often referred to as the "powerhouses of the cell," are particularly crucial in cancer cells due to their high energy demands. Mitochondrial fusion-fission dynamics play a critical role in regulating signaling pathways and metabolic activities in colorectal cancer (CRC) cells. Increased mitochondrial fission drives metabolic reprogramming, enabling CRCs to proliferate, metastasize, a
summary_bullets: Hematopoietic stem cell-conditioned media triggers excessive mitochondrial fission in colorectal cancer cells via Drp-1.
This fission disrupts the metabolic reprogramming CRC cells rely on to proliferate and metastasize.
Points to HSC-secreted factors as a potential anti-metabolic strategy against colorectal cancer.

papers.title: Bexobrutideg: A Selective, Catalytic Degrader of Bruton's Tyrosine Kinase Overcomes Inhibitor Resistance and Suppresses Autoantibody-Mediated Disease
papers.authors: Noviski, M., Auger, P., Bautista, D., Brathaban, N., Bravo, B., Cass, R., Cherala, G., Fung, T. C., Gajewski, S., Haria, D., Jiang, Z., Karr, D., Kelly, A., Kato, D., Konst, Z. A., Kumar, A., Lavarias, M., Ma, J., Marchioni, F., McIntosh, J., McKinnell, J., Mihalic, J. T., Mukerji, R., Murphy, B., Narasappa, N., Peng, G., Reddy, P. J., Robbins, D. W., Rountree, R., Singh, S., Tan, Y. S., Tenn-McClellan, A., Weiss, D. R., Wu, J., Ye, J., Yung, S., Messmer, D., Guiducci, C., Sands, A. T., Hansen, G. M., Cohen, F.
papers.abstract: Brutons tyrosine kinase (BTK) transduces B-cell receptor (BCR), Toll-like receptor (TLR), and Fc receptor (FcR) signaling, and overactivation of these pathways drives B-cell malignancies and antibody-mediated autoimmune disease. Small molecule inhibitors block the enzymatic functions of BTK, but this inhibition is undermined by resistance mutations, several of which abolish BTKs kinase activity ye
summary_bullets: Bexobrutideg is a selective catalytic degrader of BTK, rather than a classic enzymatic inhibitor.
Overcomes resistance mutations that block small-molecule BTK inhibitors from working.
Suppresses autoantibody-mediated disease, suggesting use in B-cell malignancies and autoimmune conditions.

papers.title: Decoding the Plasma Proteomic Landscape of Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Reveals Diagnostic and Prognostic Liquid Biopsy Biomarkers
papers.authors: Lakshminarayanan, H., Rutishauser, D., Schraml, P., Eberli, D., Bolck, H., Moch, H.
papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) remains the most lethal urological malignancy, with high metastatic rates, both at initial diagnosis and during disease progression, contributing to poor survival outcomes. Current diagnostic and prognostic approaches rely primarily on histopathology, limiting early detection of localized disease and relevant intervention for metastatic patients. Here, we pe
summary_bullets: Profiled the plasma proteome of clear cell renal cell carcinoma patients to find blood-based biomarkers.
Current ccRCC diagnosis relies on histopathology, limiting early detection of localized/metastatic disease.
Identifies candidate diagnostic and prognostic liquid biopsy biomarkers for ccRCC.

papers.title: Targeting AXL Overcomes Adaptive Resistance to KRAS Inhibition in KRAS-Driven Cancer
papers.authors: Thege, F. I., Kramer, A., Kreisz, N., Salim, I., Girum Girma, E., Welte, L., Adams, E., Pluchinsky, A., Kirschstein, E., Harder, O., Hoskins, A., Seetharaman, A., Rajapakshe, K., Makino, Y., Gunderson, A. J., Woermann, S. M., Maitra, A.
papers.abstract: Direct KRAS inhibitors have established mutant KRAS as a clinically actionable target, yet adaptive resistance remains a major barrier to durable responses. To identify therapeutically actionable resistance mechanisms, we performed an unbiased in vivo CRISPR activation screen in an autochthonous lung adenocarcinoma model, identifying the receptor tyrosine kinase AXL as a dominant adaptive resistan
summary_bullets: In vivo CRISPR activation screen in a lung adenocarcinoma model identifies AXL as a driver of resistance to KRAS inhibitors.
AXL upregulation lets KRAS-mutant tumors adapt and survive direct KRAS-targeted therapy.
Co-targeting AXL could overcome adaptive resistance and extend KRAS inhibitor efficacy.

papers.title: Spatial ligand-receptor gene annotations carry conditional heritability association across human tissues
papers.authors: Yang, C., Zhang, X., Chen, J.
papers.abstract: Methods that map genetic risk to cells do not directly test whether spatially organized ligand-receptor (LR) gene annotations carry conditional heritability association. Here we introduce EdgeMap, which scores each gene by the spatial activity of its LR contexts in spatial transcriptomics data, maps these scores alongside cell-intrinsic annotations to SNP-level LD scores, and tests both jointly ag
summary_bullets: Introduces EdgeMap, scoring genes by spatial ligand-receptor activity from spatial transcriptomics data.
Tests whether these spatially organized LR gene scores carry genetic (heritability) signal via SNP-level LD scores.
Links spatial cell-cell communication patterns to human disease genetics.

papers.title: ZNF768 regulates expression of E2F1 protein to drive G0/G1 transition and cell cycle progression
papers.authors: Devillers, R., Brisebois, B., Roy, S., Lelong, E., Poirier, A., Kolnohuz, A., Caron, D., Tav, C., Villot, R., Lessard, F., Tribouillard, L., Garand, C., Droit, A., Hussein, S., Joubert, P., Laplante, M., Elowe, S.
papers.abstract: Accurate and tightly coordinated cell cycle progression and cell proliferation are critical for development, growth and homeostasis of an organism. Recently, Zinc finger protein 768 (ZNF768) was identified as a transcription factor driving cellular proliferation, in both a p53-dependent and independent manner. ZNF768 interacts with and represses p53 functions to limit cell cycle delay. Independent
summary_bullets: ZNF768 is a transcription factor that drives cell proliferation partly by repressing p53.
Shows ZNF768 also regulates E2F1 expression to control the G0/G1 to S-phase transition.
Positions ZNF768 as a dual regulator of cell-cycle entry through both p53 and E2F1 pathways.

papers.title: Histone deacetylase activity limits the response to EZH2 inhibition-based therapy in epithelioid sarcoma and is targetable by epigenetic combination
papers.authors: Arrighetti, N., Soffientini, C., Zuco, V., Percio, S., Cleris, L., Abdulrazak Ahmed, S., Del Savio, E., Sigalotti, L., Maestro, R., Brich, S., Dagrada, G. P., Barisella, M., Collini, P., Kentsis, A., Huang, P. H., Gronchi, A., Frezza, A. M., Stacchiotti, S., Zaffaroni, N., Pasquali, S.
papers.abstract: Epithelioid sarcoma (EpS) is an aggressive ultra-rare soft tissue sarcoma (STS) driven by INI1 loss and consequent hyperactivation of the chromatin-modifying enzyme EZH2. Although the EZH2 inhibitor tazemetostat has shown clinical activity, responses remain limited, highlighting the need for improved treatment strategies. Here, using two in-house generated patient-derived xenograft models and matc
summary_bullets: EZH2 inhibitor tazemetostat has limited efficacy in epithelioid sarcoma despite EZH2 hyperactivation from INI1 loss.
HDAC activity limits tumor response to EZH2 inhibition in patient-derived xenograft models.
Combining HDAC and EZH2 inhibition is proposed as a more effective epigenetic strategy.

papers.title: Preclinical Evaluation of Chemoradiation Resistance Using 18F-FDG PET/CT in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
papers.authors: Heirman, C. C., Rickard, A. G., Castillo, R., Gonzalez, K., Pittman, A., Smith, J., Kelly, K. E., Stevens, J. B., Watts, T., Mowery, Y. M., Lafata, K. J.
papers.abstract:
PurposeThere is an urgent need for improved prognostic tools and biological understanding of chemoradiation resistance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). This study established a preclinical imaging dataset aimed at identifying prognostic imaging features from 18F-FDG micro-PET/CT scans in HNSCC mouse models.

MethodsThree orthotopic murine models were utilized: two human papillomav
summary_bullets: Built a preclinical 18F-FDG micro-PET/CT imaging dataset in orthotopic HNSCC mouse models.
Aims to identify imaging features that predict chemoradiation resistance before/during treatment.
Includes HPV-positive and HPV-negative models to capture biological subtype differences.

papers.title: Multidirectional Cellular Plasticity in Ewing Sarcoma Reveals a Tumor-CAF Continuum and Novel Immunotherapeutic Targets
papers.authors: Sharif, M. A., Khan, A. S., Brentjens, R. J., Olejniczak, S. H., Withers, H. G., Ohm, J.
papers.abstract: Ewing sarcoma (EwS) is an aggressive pediatric malignancy with poor outcomes for patients with metastatic or relapsed disease. Effective immunotherapeutic approaches, including CAR T-cell therapy, are limited by intratumoral heterogeneity, an incompletely characterized tumor microenvironment (TME), and a lack of well-defined, tumor-restricted target antigens. To address these limitations, we perfo
summary_bullets: Reveals a continuum between Ewing sarcoma tumor cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), not a fixed cell-type boundary.
Multidirectional cellular plasticity contributes to intratumoral heterogeneity that limits CAR T-cell therapy.
Identifies novel tumor-restricted antigens as candidate immunotherapy targets.

papers.title: A collaborative submission model for building high-quality data resources at scale through partnership
papers.authors: Hilton, J. A., Chaffer, J., Chien, J., Gabdank, I., Mott, B., Rutherford, E., Small, C., Zamanian, J., Aevermann, B., Cherry, J. M., Klein, T. E.
papers.abstract: Community data resources that aggregate datasets across studies are critical infrastructure for modern biomedical research, accelerating discovery as rapidly advancing Artificial Intelligence (AI) models place ever-greater demand on large, well-described data corpora. However, building these resources involves a fundamental tension: comprehensive metadata is imperative for reuse, yet capturing thi
summary_bullets: Describes a collaborative model for building large, high-quality biomedical data resources via partnership rather than solo curation.
Balances the tension between rich metadata (needed for reuse) and the burden of capturing it.
Relevant as AI models increasingly demand large, well-described data corpora.

papers.title: HIV-1 Hijacks HGF/c-MET Signaling to Promote Viral Entry and Replication in Primary CD4⁺ T Cells
papers.authors: Tripathi, S., Allen, M. M., Wu, L.
papers.abstract: The mesenchymal-epithelial transition factor (c-MET) is a receptor tyrosine kinase best known for mediating hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) signaling in cancer, yet its role in HIV-1 infection remains undefined. Here we identify c-MET as a host factor that facilitates HIV-1 replication in CD4+ T cells by promoting viral entry. HIV-1 infection upregulates c-MET transcripts and phosphorylation in pri
summary_bullets: Identifies c-MET, previously known mainly in cancer, as a host factor exploited by HIV-1.
HIV-1 infection upregulates and activates c-MET in CD4+ T cells to promote viral entry.
Suggests c-MET-targeting drugs already used in oncology could be repurposed against HIV.

papers.title: Pervasive Backdoor Vulnerabilities in Genomic Foundation Models
papers.authors: Ni, S., Wang, Q., Wei, C., Ni, X., Li, S., Zhao, Z., Li, H., Ji, R., Wang, T., Yang, M.
papers.abstract: Genomic foundation models are increasingly used to interpret and design DNA sequences, yet their susceptibility to training-data manipulation remains poorly understood. Here we systematically evaluate backdoor poisoning across three model families, seven parameter scales ranging from 50 million to 7 billion, and 18 genomic classification tasks. We introduce two complementary 48-nucleotide triggers
summary_bullets: Systematically tests backdoor data-poisoning attacks across 3 model families, 7 sizes (50M-7B params), and 18 genomic tasks.
Genomic foundation models are broadly vulnerable to training-data manipulation via short 48-nucleotide triggers.
Raises security concerns for deploying genomic AI models trained on public or untrusted data.

papers.title: Explainable HGT-based framework for predicting human dark kinase protein-pathway associations by leveraging BERT-based embeddings and WGAN-GP
papers.authors: Dutta, S., Mitra, P.
papers.abstract: Discovery of pathway associations and druggability can leverage underutililized dark kinase genes for treating complex diseases (proven for cancer and neurodegeneration), boosted with computational methods. Herein, we employ BERT-based embeddings of proteins and pathways (refined via two-stage transformer and heterogeneous graph transformer) and protein-protein and protein-pathway associations- bo
summary_bullets: Uses BERT-based embeddings and a heterogeneous graph transformer to predict pathway associations for understudied "dark kinases".
Combines protein-protein and protein-pathway network data with generative augmentation (WGAN-GP).
Framework is explainable, aiming to make dark kinase druggability predictions more interpretable.

papers.title: Omega-S: A Functional Resilience Index for LLM Fine-Tuning
papers.authors: Alberto Acedo
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning a large language model on new data degrades what it previously learned. We present Omega-S, a drop-in penalty computed from the weight matrix alone: it needs no previous-task data, no Fisher matrix and no stored copy of the old weights. It is three lines in an existing training loop and adds under 4% to the cost of a step. Retention. On Llama-3-8B with LoRA, fine-tuned from code to pro
summary_bullets: Omega-S is a lightweight penalty term that reduces catastrophic forgetting during LLM fine-tuning.
Needs no old training data, Fisher matrix, or stored copy of prior weights -- just the weight matrix.
Adds under 4% compute overhead and improves retention of prior capabilities (tested on Llama-3-8B/LoRA).

papers.title: Want to get more from AI? Treat every prompt like an experiment
papers.authors: Dewar JM.
summary_bullets: Nature commentary argues researchers should approach AI prompting with the same rigor as a scientific experiment.
Encourages systematic testing and iteration to get more reliable, useful outputs from AI tools.

papers.title: Uncovering ectopic GC-like niches for tumor reactive lymphocyte priming in lung adenocarcinoma using Stereo-XCR-seq
papers.authors: Zhan X, Huang M, Zhang Y, Liu Z, Liu C, Guo Y, Liu Y, Zhou W, Yan Y, Zeng H, Dong Y, Dong X, Chen X, Yang H, Ma R, Zhu F, Zheng X, Li X, Hou S, Gao Z, Yin J, Chan FK, Wu Q, Deng S, Yao Y, Suo S, Liu C, Liu L, Xu X, Hou Y, Tao H, Ai X, Dong Y, Zeng T, Sun H, Li Y, Zuo L, Wang H, Liu X, Wu Z, Zhou J, Zeng Z, Feng Y.
papers.abstract: T/B cell receptors (T/BCR), coordinating antigen-targeting immune response, play crucial roles in anti-tumor immune response. Tracking T and B cell clonal evolution in situ at single-cell resolution is essential for understanding the adaptive immune responses. To address the lack of tools for in situ single-cell T/BCR (XCR) sequencing, we develop Stereo-XCR-seq, an efficient method for retrieving
summary_bullets: Develops Stereo-XCR-seq, an in situ single-cell method for spatially resolved T/B-cell receptor (TCR/BCR) sequencing.
Reveals ectopic germinal-center-like niches in lung adenocarcinoma that prime tumor-reactive lymphocytes.
Enables tracking of clonal immune cell evolution directly within the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: A foundation model for sleep-based risk stratification and clinical outcomes
papers.authors: Bilal E, Araujo MLD, Beck KL, Heinzinger CM, Ghosn S, Saab CY, Foldvary-Schaefer N, Rogers JL, Mehra R.
papers.abstract: Clinical sleep studies capture multiple physiologic signals, yet interpretation is often reduced to single summary measures of limited prognostic value, such as the apnea-hypopnea index. We present a foundation model that learns rich representations of sleep physiology from more than 10,000 clinical sleep recordings linked to electronic medical records. Here we show that sleep physiology contains
summary_bullets: Built a foundation model trained on over 10,000 clinical sleep recordings linked to electronic medical records.
Moves beyond single summary metrics (like apnea-hypopnea index) to richer sleep-physiology representations.
Enables better risk stratification and prediction of clinical outcomes from sleep data.

papers.title: Ultrarapid deep 3D histology enables intraoperative mapping of glioma infiltration
papers.authors: Liu Z, Li Y, Chen L, Wei M, Wei M, Sun Y, Wang T, Cheng H, Liu X, Ji M, Shi L.
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) histology provides volumetric insights into tissue microarchitectures across entire specimens, holding great promise for more accurate prognostication. However, existing methods are too slow for intraoperative consultations. We present ULTRA (ultrarapid cleared stimulated Raman with AI), a label-free, stain-free, fixation-free, and section-free platform that leverages the ch
summary_bullets: ULTRA is a label-free, stain-free, fixation-free 3D histology platform using stimulated Raman scattering plus AI.
Fast enough for intraoperative use, unlike existing 3D histology methods.
Enables real-time mapping of glioma infiltration margins during surgery.

papers.title: Privacy risks from medical AI tools are not shared equally
papers.authors: Zhang H, Ghassemi M.
summary_bullets: Nature commentary highlights that privacy risks from medical AI tools fall disproportionately on certain patient groups.
Calls attention to equity considerations often overlooked in medical AI deployment and data use.

papers.title: This AI Raygun can shrink and supersize proteins - opening the door to easy editing
papers.authors: Conroy G.
summary_bullets: News piece on "Raygun," an AI tool that can shrink or enlarge natural proteins while preserving function.
Framed as opening new possibilities for easier, more flexible protein engineering.

papers.title: SPEN Loss Drives Extrafollicular Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma with Female-Specific Lethality and Therapeutic Vulnerabilities
papers.authors: Pelzer B, Meydan C, Spiegel IM, Karagiannidis I, Xia M, Teater M, Welter EM, Searcy ZE, Hilton LK, Barisic D, Fong A, Fa P, Sethi S, Isgor IS, Fielding JJ, Karbalayghareh A, Burdette CS, Tumuluru S, Debek SM, Lee S, Massoni-Badosa R, Durmaz C, Salataj E, Pararajalingam P, Chen Z, Pelzl RJ, Shah S, Rivas MA, Hoehn KB, Mlynarczyk C, Isles HM, Wang X, Dogan A, Elenitoba-Johnson KSJ, Scott DW, Dreval K, Morin RD, Leslie CS, Puri R, Geri JB, Chin CR, Chadburn A, Mason CE, Reinhardt HC, Anguera MC, Béguelin W, Venturutti L, Melnick AM.
papers.abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphomas (DLBCL) are genetically and phenotypically heterogeneous, making diagnosis and treatment challenging. Current models suggest DLBCLs derive from follicular B cells engaged in adaptive immune responses. By studying cooccurring truncating mutations in SPEN and NOTCH2 in the BN2-DLBCL subtype, our data suggest a previously unrecognized extrafollicular trajectory. Using a
summary_bullets: SPEN and NOTCH2 co-occurring truncating mutations define a previously unrecognized extrafollicular DLBCL trajectory.
This SPEN-loss DLBCL subtype shows female-specific lethality.
Identifies therapeutic vulnerabilities specific to this newly defined lymphoma subtype.

papers.title: Same-Slide Spatial Multiomics Integration with IN-DEPTH Reveals Tumor Virus-Linked Spatial Reorganization of the Tumor Microenvironment
papers.authors: Yiu SPT, Chang Y, Yeo YY, Qiu H, Wu W, Michel HA, Jin X, Huang R, Kure S, Parmelee L, Luo S, Cramer P, Lee JL, Wang Y, Zhao Z, Yeung J, El Ahmar N, Simsek B, Mohanna R, Van Orden M, Lu WS, Livak KJ, Li S, Gao C, Burgess M, Keane C, Shahryari J, Kingsley LG, Al-Humadi RN, Nasr S, Nkosi D, Sadigh S, Rock P, Frauenfeld L, Kaufmann L, Zhu B, Basak A, Dhanikonda N, Chan CN, Krull J, Cho YW, Chen CY, Brown J, Wang H, Zhao B, Lee JJ, Loo LH, Kim DM, Boussiotis VA, Zhang B, Wei K, Shalek AK, Howitt BE, Signoretti S, Schürch CM, Hodi FS, Burack WR, Rodig SJ, Ma Q, Jiang S.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics and proteomics have enabled profound insights into tissue organization, yet these technologies remain largely disparate, and emerging same-slide multiomics approaches are limited in plex, spatial resolution, signal retention, and integrative analytics. We introduce IN-situ DEtailed Phenotyping To High-resolution transcriptomics (IN-DEPTH), a streamlined, resource-efficient,
summary_bullets: IN-DEPTH combines spatial transcriptomics and proteomics on the same tissue slide, improving on disparate single-modality methods.
Reveals tumor-virus-linked spatial reorganization of the tumor microenvironment.
Designed to be streamlined and resource-efficient for broader adoption.

papers.title: CellTune: an integrative software for accurate cell classification in spatial proteomics
papers.authors: Bussi Y, Shainshein D, Ovits E, Posner S, Azulay N, Maimon N, Keidar Haran T, Ben-Uri R, Brown C, Schuldiner N, Yaniv E, Van Valen D, Milo I, Elhanani O, Schiemann R, Keren L.
papers.abstract: Spatial proteomics measures multiple proteins in situ, capturing tissue complexity. However, cell classification in densely packed tissues remains challenging because of the lack of efficient classification algorithms, annotation tools and high-quality labeled datasets to benchmark computational methods. We introduce CellTune, an integrated software for analysis of large spatial proteomics dataset
summary_bullets: CellTune is integrative software for accurate cell classification in densely packed spatial proteomics data.
Addresses the lack of efficient algorithms, annotation tools, and benchmark datasets in the field.
Aims to standardize and improve cell-type calling across spatial proteomics platforms.

papers.title: SpaMTP: integrative statistical analysis and visualization of spatial metabolomics and transcriptomics data
papers.authors: Causer A, Lu T, Kriel J, Moffet JJD, Fitzgerald CCJ, Newman A, Vu H, Tan X, Vo T, Cui C, Narayana VK, Whittle JR, Best SA, Freytag S, Nguyen Q.
papers.abstract: Spatially resolved multimodal data enable the exploration of transcriptional, proteomic and metabolic regulation, yet analytical tools to integrate these spatial omics modalities, particularly spatial metabolomics, remain limited. We developed SpaMTP, an end-to-end framework that implements functions within a common Seurat architecture. It introduces analyses for metabolite annotation, joint clust
summary_bullets: SpaMTP integrates spatial metabolomics and transcriptomics analysis within the familiar Seurat framework.
Adds tools for metabolite annotation, joint clustering, and cross-modality visualization.
Fills a gap left by existing tools that don't handle spatial metabolomics well.

papers.title: Author Correction: Cucurbituril-based anion-conducting membranes with supramolecular nanopores
papers.authors: Xu Z, Lin D, Yin H, Feng Q, Foglia F, Zhen Y, Morris A, Berrod Q, Pang M, Huang L, Liu J, Tian J, Wang X, Yang C, Tang X, Zhang X, Wang B, Wang H, Liu K.
summary_bullets: Published correction to a paper on cucurbituril-based anion-conducting membranes with supramolecular nanopores.
No new scientific findings; amends or clarifies details of the original report.

papers.title: End-to-end multimodal pathology foundation model with clinical dialogue
papers.authors: Vorontsov E, Shaikovski G, Casson A, Viret J, Zimmermann E, Tenenholtz N, Wang YK, Bernhard JH, Godrich RA, Retamero JA, Shia J, Gonen M, Weiser MR, Klimstra DS, Yousfi R, Fusi N, Fuchs TJ, Severson K, Liu S.
papers.abstract: Recent rapid progress in the field of computational pathology has been enabled by foundation models. These models are beginning to move beyond encoding image patches toward whole-slide understanding, but their clinical utility remains limited. Here we present PRISM2, a multimodal slide-level foundation model trained on 2.3 million whole-slide images and 14 million question-answer pairs derived fro
summary_bullets: PRISM2 is a multimodal, slide-level pathology foundation model trained on 2.3M whole-slide images and 14M Q&A pairs.
Moves beyond patch-level image encoding toward whole-slide, dialogue-capable understanding.
Aims to improve clinical utility of computational pathology through interactive, clinically grounded outputs.

papers.title: Scientists using LLMs will 'do more, less well', modelling study predicts
papers.authors: Glickman K.
summary_bullets: Modelling study predicts scientists using LLMs will increase output but reduce quality/rigor per study.
Raises concerns about an AI-driven productivity/quality trade-off in research.

papers.title: Mapping micrometastatic seeds of relapse
papers.authors: Yeo HTG, Tan IB.
papers.abstract: In this issue of Cancer Cell, Liu et al. apply spatial multi-omics to map colorectal cancer micrometastases across primary tumors and matched liver and lung metastases, revealing liver micrometastases as an early evolved, stem-like, immune-suppressed residual disease state linked to a six-gene recurrence signature.
summary_bullets: Commentary on a study applying spatial multi-omics to colorectal cancer micrometastases in liver and lung.
Liver micrometastases appear as an early, stem-like, immune-suppressed residual disease state.
This state links to a six-gene signature predicting recurrence risk.

papers.title: Spatial atlas of the human brain vasculature reveals specialized cell ensembles
papers.authors: Wang JC, Sanchez D, Arul S, Gülsuyu B, Gopinadhan A, Mukhtar T, Kim J, Andrews JP, Alonso Cee Williams M, Jung Y, Hashimoto ML, Kim CN, Bhalla S, Ewing-Crystal NA, Bernabei JM, Letchuman V, Haddad AF, Hemphill K, Weinsheimer SM, Kim H, Narsinh KH, Cooke DL, Cadwell CR, Wälchli T, Elahi FM, Yang AC, He P, Chang EF, Molofsky AB, Winkler EA.
papers.abstract: The brain vasculature comprises diverse specialized cells that are essential for brain function, yet their spatial organization remains poorly understood. Here, we construct a comprehensive cerebrovascular cell atlas encompassing 314,535 transcriptomes that captures the arteriovenous axis and defines consensus cell states. We then perform spatial transcriptomics to map 1,529,740 cells across the h
summary_bullets: Built a cerebrovascular cell atlas of over 314,000 transcriptomes spanning the human brain's arteriovenous axis.
Spatial transcriptomics mapped over 1.5 million cells to their vascular locations across the brain.
Reveals specialized, spatially organized vascular cell ensembles supporting brain function.

papers.title: AI-driven discovery and validation of a GIPC1 PDZ domain inhibitor for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
papers.authors: Rachamala HK, Rao Nakka NM, Angom RS, Varanasi SM, Wei F, Kulkarni T, Dutta SK, Wang E, Kulkarni NM, Geoffrey A S B, Hegde SP, Perumal S, Gurram K, Gharibi H, Gaetani M, Mukherjee SP, Babiker H, Pal K, Mukhopadhyay D.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains highly aggressive, with a five-year survival rate under 13.3%, due to late diagnosis, rapid progression, and therapeutic resistance, highlighting the need for advanced treatments. GAIP-interacting protein C terminus 1 (GIPC1), a scaffolding protein overexpressed in PDAC, drives tumor growth and chemoresistance but has remained "undruggable" due to it
summary_bullets: GIPC1, an "undruggable" scaffolding protein, drives PDAC tumor growth and chemoresistance.
Used AI-driven discovery to find a small-molecule inhibitor targeting GIPC1's PDZ domain.
Validates a new therapeutic candidate for a cancer with under 13.3% five-year survival.

papers.title: Human-inspired time-series health evaluation with an adaptive multimodal electronic skin
papers.authors: Xu C, Zheng H, Heng W, Liu R, MarionSims J, Li J, Jin P, Tay RY, Min J, Wang G, Yue Y, Gao W.
papers.abstract: Electronic skin powered with artificial intelligence could enable next-generation robotic and medical devices, yet integrating multimodal sensors and analyzing heterogeneous, multifrequency time series remain challenging. Most wearable machine learning architectures are time-invariant and trained for a specific task, limiting transfer across modalities and users. We present a multimodal electronic
summary_bullets: Developed a multimodal, AI-powered electronic skin for time-series health monitoring.
Adaptive architecture transfers across sensing modalities and users, unlike prior time-invariant wearable ML.
Enables human-inspired, continuous health evaluation for next-gen wearable and robotic devices.

papers.title: Author Correction: Sleep chart of biological ageing clocks in middle and late life
papers.authors: MULTI Consortium, O'Toole CK, Song Z, Anagnostakis F, Yang Z, Tian YE, Duggan MR, Zou C, Leng Y, Cai Y, Bai W, Fu CHY, Rafii MS, Aisen P, Wang G, De Jager PL, Zeng J, Oh HS, Zhou X, Walker KA, Belsky DW, Zalesky A, Simonsick EM, Resnick SM, Ferrucci L, Davatzikos C, Wen J.
summary_bullets: Published correction to a large multi-cohort study of biological ageing clocks across middle and late life sleep.
Amends details of the original "sleep chart of biological ageing clocks" report.

papers.title: Inference of secreted protein signaling activities in intercellular communication
papers.authors: Ru B, Gong L, Yang E, Park S, Zaki G, Aldape K, Wakefield L, Jiang P.
papers.abstract: The human genome encodes ~1,900 secreted proteins, many of which mediate intercellular communication. Secreted proteins do not act cell-autonomously, limiting systematic approaches to characterize their functions. Here we introduce SecAct (Secreted Activity, https://secact.ccr.cancer.gov ), a computational framework that infers the signaling activities of 1,170 human secreted proteins from spatial
summary_bullets: SecAct infers signaling activity of 1,170 human secreted proteins from spatial and transcriptomic data.
Addresses the challenge that secreted proteins act non-cell-autonomously, complicating standard analysis.
Provides a computational framework and public tool for studying intercellular communication via secreted factors.

papers.title: Mediators of cell fate decisions in human fetal kidney development identified using spatial transcriptomics
summary_bullets: Nature Genetics piece on mediators of cell fate decisions in human fetal kidney development, identified via spatial transcriptomics.
Companion to related work directly mapping kidney developmental cell-fate decisions.

papers.title: Single-cell spatial mapping of human kidney development implicates the microenvironment in guiding cell fate decisions
papers.authors: Levinsohn J, Grindel S, Dumoulin B, Abedini A, Conte C, Huang AZ, Levin-Klein R, Weisz B, Rabinowitz G, Bergeson AM, Ha E, Klötzer KA, Zhang N, Titchenell P, Li M, Park JS, Arroyo JP, Finn LS, Sasaki K, Beckerman P, Pleniceanu O, Romagnani P, Hughes AJ, Susztak K.
papers.abstract: Evolution has used cell-cell communication as a strategy to coordinate organ development, enabling the reproducible generation of intricate structures. Classically, these interactions have been studied one at a time in model organisms, limiting our understanding of how cellular interplay coordinates human development. We investigated human kidney development using single-cell RNA sequencing and sp
summary_bullets: Single-cell RNA-seq plus spatial profiling of human kidney development reveals cell-cell communication driving fate decisions.
Shows the microenvironment actively guides which cell fates progenitor cells adopt.
Moves beyond model-organism studies to directly characterize human kidney developmental signaling.

papers.title: Decadal sink-source shifts of forest aboveground carbon since 1988
papers.authors: Qian Z, Bathiany S, Liu T, Blaschke LL, Teo HC, Boers N.
papers.abstract: Forest ecosystems are vital to the global carbon cycle, yet their long-term aboveground carbon (AGC) dynamics remain uncertain. Here, we integrate multi-source satellite observations with probabilistic deep learning models to reconstruct a harmonized, uncertainty-aware global forest AGC record from 1988 to 2021 at 0.25<sup>∘</sup>. We find that, although global forests sequestered 6.2 PgC, moist t
summary_bullets: Combined satellite data with probabilistic deep learning to reconstruct global forest carbon dynamics from 1988-2021.
Global forests sequestered 6.2 PgC overall, but moist tropical forests show shifting sink/source behavior.
Provides an uncertainty-aware, long-term record of how forest carbon storage is changing.

papers.title: Escaping our own biases: AI, scientific reasoning, and discovery in molecular biology
papers.authors: Costa TRD, Penadés JR.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence may transform molecular biology not by always providing the correct answer, but by exploring mechanistic possibilities unconstrained by the assumptions that shape expert thinking. Its greatest contribution may be exposing the intellectual blind spots of scientists, while experimental validation remains the ultimate arbiter of truth.
summary_bullets: Commentary argues AI's value in molecular biology may lie in exploring possibilities beyond expert assumptions, not just giving correct answers.
AI can expose scientists' intellectual blind spots, but experiments remain the final arbiter of truth.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal multiomics uncover tumor ecosystem dynamics during metastatic colonization
papers.authors: Sun Y, Zhong Y, Liu S, Zhang Z, Wang C, Liu Y, Chen J, Guo W, Gu X, Rao K, Wang Z, Cao M, Wang Y, Huang W, Zou X, Chen X, Qiu S, Shi Y, Sun H, Huang X, Wang Y, Wang J, Wu Z, Tian R, Zhang Y, Gu J, Jiang M, Bai Y, Li G, Xie M, Xi F, Peng L, Liu S, Yang S, Zhang Y, Esteban MA, Jin X, Chen A, Wang J, Cang Y, Peng DH, Xu X, Zhou J, Wu L, Fan J.
papers.abstract: The mechanisms underlying the interactions between disseminated tumor cells (DTCs) and their tissue microenvironment during metastatic colonization are currently poorly understood. We integrated multimodal single-cell and spatial profiling from liver cancer mouse models and human metastases to track the spatiotemporal dynamics of DTCs and their microenvironments from single-cell seeding to overt l
summary_bullets: Integrated single-cell and spatial profiling of liver cancer mouse models and human metastases.
Tracks disseminated tumor cells and their microenvironment from single-cell seeding to overt metastasis.
Reveals dynamic tumor-microenvironment interactions driving metastatic colonization over time.

papers.title: Gene regulatory innovations from transposable elements in primate cerebellum development
papers.authors: Yamada T, Sepp M, Sarropoulos I, Kaessmann H.
papers.abstract: Transposable elements are hypothesized to have driven gene regulatory innovation, yet their contributions to primate brain development at the cell type level remain underexplored. Here, we use single-cell multiomics data from human, macaque, marmoset, and mouse cerebella to show that transposable element contributions to different cell types are shaped by varying degrees of constraints across cell
summary_bullets: Compared single-cell multiomics across human, macaque, marmoset, and mouse cerebellum development.
Transposable elements contribute to gene regulatory innovation in a cell-type-specific manner.
Degree of TE-driven regulatory contribution varies with evolutionary constraint across cell types.

papers.title: Deep learning segmentation with curvature consistency reveals astrocyte nanostructure across species
papers.authors: Fok AHK, Wang Y, Ng M, Syed T, Wong TYM, Salmon CK, Salathiel T, Grondin-Eddy W, Fan L, Siddiqi K, Murai KK.
papers.abstract: Cellular function depends on the precise deployment and distribution of nanoscale structures, but these features remain difficult to measure and compare between cells and datasets. This challenge is pronounced for astrocytes, whose intricate nanostructures interface with neurons, glia, and vasculature, to control brain development, synaptic development/plasticity, homeostasis, and responses to inj
summary_bullets: Developed a curvature-consistent deep learning segmentation method for nanoscale cell structures.
Applied to astrocytes, whose fine nanostructures are hard to measure and compare across datasets and species.
Enables cross-species comparison of astrocyte nanostructure relevant to brain development and disease.

papers.title: Miniaturizing and modifying natural proteins with Raygun
papers.authors: Devkota K, Shonai D, Mao J, Ko YS, Wang W, Soderling S, Singh R.
papers.abstract: Proteins have evolved over billions of years through coordinated substitutions, insertions and deletions, yet computational protein design cannot fully replicate nature's ability to engineer new proteins from existing templates. Protein language models<sup>1-3</sup> generate informative per-residue representations, but harnessing them for large-scale, function-preserving sequence modifications has
summary_bullets: Raygun uses protein language model representations to enable large-scale, function-preserving protein redesign.
Can miniaturize or otherwise modify natural proteins while retaining their function.
Advances computational protein engineering beyond fixed per-residue predictions.

papers.title: Parallel nonlinear neuromorphic computing with temporal encoding
papers.authors: You G, Qian C, Wu O, Chen H.
papers.abstract: The proliferation of deep learning applications has intensified the demand for electronic hardware with low energy consumption and fast computing speed. Neuromorphic photonics have emerged as a viable alternative to process high-throughput information at the physical space. However, the simultaneous attainment of high linear and nonlinear expressivity poses a considerable challenge due to the powe
summary_bullets: Demonstrates parallel nonlinear neuromorphic computing using temporal (time-based) encoding.
Neuromorphic photonics offer a low-energy, high-speed alternative to conventional electronic hardware.
Addresses the tradeoff between linear and nonlinear expressivity in photonic neuromorphic systems.

papers.title: Integrating structurally defined DNA-carbon nanotube sensors with machine learning for cancer detection
papers.authors: Chen P, Zheng X, Li Y, Li J, Zhou X, Wen Y, Liu J, Wang P, Li X, Chen R, Lin Z.
papers.abstract: Liquid biopsy is a promising, noninvasive approach for cancer detection, but current methods often trade off accuracy, operability, and cost. To address these limitations, we introduce an artificial perception system (APS) for liquid biopsy that combines a structurally defined DNA-carbon nanotube sensor array with machine learning (ML) models. The array produces multichannel fluorescence fingerpri
summary_bullets: Built an "artificial perception system" combining DNA-carbon nanotube sensor arrays with machine learning.
Produces multichannel fluorescence fingerprints for noninvasive liquid biopsy cancer detection.
Aims to improve on existing liquid biopsy methods that trade off accuracy, ease of use, and cost.

papers.title: Organelle proteomics of human, neonatal pig, healthy and diabetic mouse islets
papers.authors: Caliskan ÖS, Haas DT, Ferreira JV, Chubanava S, Kemter E, Cota P, Bastidas-Ponce A, Tarquis-Medina M, Czarnecki O, Bhattacharya S, Jaki J, Geiger V, Kakimoto P, Brandt D, Sachser M, Dürr C, Delgado de la Herran H, Cebrian-Serrano A, Müller TD, Wolf E, Lickert H, Bakhti M, Krahmer N.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic islets, in which β cells constitute 50%-80% of the endocrine mass, are the body's site for glucose-regulated insulin secretion. Pancreatic islet dysfunction is a hallmark of type 2 diabetes. Nevertheless, the molecular changes that impair their function remain insufficiently understood. To determine how islet cellular organization supports function and how it deteriorates in disease, we
summary_bullets: Compared organelle proteomes across human, neonatal pig, and healthy vs. diabetic mouse pancreatic islets.
Beta cells make up 50-80% of islet mass and are central to insulin secretion.
Aims to reveal molecular changes in islet organization that underlie type 2 diabetes dysfunction.

papers.title: AI proteomics: from protein identification to virtual cells
papers.authors: Sun Y, A J, Liu Z, Sun R, Qian L, Payne SH, Bittremieux W, Ralser M, Li C, Chen Y, Dong Z, Perez-Riverol Y, Khan A, Sander C, Aebersold R, Vizcaíno JA, Krieger JR, Yao J, Han W, Zhang L, Zhu Y, Xuan Y, Sun BB, Qiao L, Hermjakob H, Tang H, Gao H, Deng Y, Zhong Q, Chang C, Bandeira N, Li M, E W, Sun S, Yang Y, Omenn GS, Zhang Y, Xu P, Fu Y, Liu X, Overall CM, Wang Y, Deutsch EW, Chen L, Cox J, Demichev V, He F, Huang J, Jin H, Liu C, Li N, Luan Z, Song J, Yu K, Wan W, Wang T, Zhang K, Zhang L, Bell PA, Mann M, Zhang B, Guo T.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming scientific research, including proteomics. In this Perspective, we highlight key mass spectrometry (MS)-based proteomics areas where AI is driving innovation, ranging from protein identification to building AI virtual cells. These include improving peptide and protein identification and quantification; characterizing protein-protein interactions and pro
summary_bullets: Perspective on how AI is transforming mass-spectrometry-based proteomics, from ID to "virtual cells".
Covers AI's role in peptide/protein identification, quantification, and characterizing protein interactions.
Frames proteomics AI advances as a step toward building comprehensive virtual cell models.

papers.title: Paired mutation calling and spatial transcriptomics identify cellular neighborhoods associated with the neoplastic outcome of mouse colitis
papers.authors: Moutin EB, Chang LLH, Giavara G, Mehmed S, Colombé M, Boquetale C, Marks K, Lourenço FC, Skoufou-Papoutsaki N, Kemp R, Gascard P, Tlsty TD, Tourigny DS, Winton DJ.
papers.abstract: In the progression from inflammatory bowel disease to associated cancer, the clonal mutational landscape shifts from selection of mutations in inflammatory genes to selection for cancer-driver mutations. How prevalence and expansion of either type of mutant clones could be impacted by the cellular environments in which they arise and how this affects the neoplastic outcome of colitis remains unkno
summary_bullets: Combines mutation calling with spatial transcriptomics to study neoplastic progression in mouse colitis.
Tracks how the clonal mutational landscape shifts from inflammatory to cancer-driver mutations.
Shows local cellular neighborhoods influence which mutant clones expand toward cancer.

papers.title: Machine learning reveals biocontrol agents shaping disease outcome in natural Arabidopsis populations
papers.authors: Mahmoudi M, Hu Y, Almario J, Stincone P, Tenzer LM, Chaudhry V, Braun L, Quinzer S, Nieselt K, Kemen E.
papers.abstract: Plants recruit antagonistic microbes to defend against phytopathogens, offering a route to rational biocontrol beyond empirical screening. Here, using six generations of leaf-microbiome data from natural Arabidopsis populations infected by the oomycete Albugo laibachii, we show that microbial diversity is driven by infection, site, and host genotype, and that infected plants form modular networks
summary_bullets: Used six generations of leaf microbiome data from natural Arabidopsis populations infected by an oomycete pathogen.
Machine learning identifies specific biocontrol agents shaping disease outcome.
Microbial diversity is driven by infection, site, and host genotype, forming modular defensive networks.

papers.title: Why machines don't speak biology: Toward native biological language models
papers.authors: Stelzer Y, Tanay A.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in AI inspire visions of universal models of biology. Yet living systems are evolved, emergent processes whose behaviors cannot be inferred from their parts alone. We propose grounding AI in canonical biological processes, constructing data-driven world models with explicit mechanistic links across molecules, cells, and their dynamics in space and time.
summary_bullets: Argues living systems are evolved, emergent processes that can't be fully captured by inferring from parts alone.
Proposes grounding AI in canonical biological processes rather than generic universal models.
Advocates building data-driven "world models" with explicit mechanistic links across scales.
